title: Closing costs when buying a home in Ontario: what to budget for
excerpt: Beyond the down payment: the closing costs Niagara buyers should plan for, and how to avoid surprises on closing day.
content:
Your down payment is the biggest number you'll save for, but it isn't the only one. Closing costs are the fees and taxes due when the home officially becomes yours, and they can add up quickly if you haven't planned for them.

Land transfer tax

In Ontario, buyers pay a provincial land transfer tax based on the purchase price. It's usually the largest closing cost. First-time buyers may qualify for a rebate, so ask your lawyer to confirm what applies to you.

Legal fees and disbursements

A real estate lawyer handles the title search, registers the transfer and manages the funds on closing. Expect a legal fee plus disbursements for searches and registration. Get a written quote before you commit.

Title insurance

Most lenders require title insurance, which protects against issues such as title fraud, errors in surveys or unpaid work orders on the property.

Home inspection and appraisal

A home inspection is one of the best investments you can make before firming up an offer. Your lender may also order an appraisal, which is sometimes billed to the buyer.

Adjustments

If the seller has prepaid property taxes or utilities past the closing date, you'll reimburse them for your share. Your lawyer calculates these adjustments in the statement of adjustments.

Moving and setup

Don't forget movers, utility hookups, home insurance (required before closing if you have a mortgage) and any immediate repairs or furniture.

How to avoid surprises

  • Ask your lender and lawyer for estimates early in the process
  • Keep a buffer in your budget beyond the down payment
  • Review your statement of adjustments a few days before closing
